page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers relative to modern hardware. The Intel Skylake-era processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (specifically avx512f and avx512_vnni) and AES cryptography. However, stress-ng CPU benchmarks yield 1103.19 for single-core and 2934.5 for multi-core performance, both falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show a sharp decline from 164.06 GB/sec for small cached blocks to 20.58 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, indicating potential bottlenecks during memory-intensive operations.

The instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c5.xlarge offers dedicated CPU resources at a lower entry point, making it suitable for workloads that require predictable CPU allocation without massive memory demands. Given its benchmark profile, it is best suited for light compute tasks, basic web serving (achieving 3.36 GB/sec static web throughput), small-scale Redis deployments (processing 2.86 million SET operations per second), and lightweight microservices rather than high-performance computing or large-scale data processing.
